From 426ca15c7f6cb6562a081341ca88893a50c59fa2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jibin Zhang <jibin.zhang@mediatek.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 23:21:11 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: fix segmentation of forwarding fraglist GRO

This patch enhances GSO segment handling by properly checking
the SKB_GSO_DODGY flag for frag_list GSO packets, addressing
low throughput issues observed when a station accesses IPv4
servers via hotspots with an IPv6-only upstream interface.

Specifically, it fixes a bug in GSO segmentation when forwarding
GRO packets containing a frag_list. The function skb_segment_list
cannot correctly process GRO skbs that have been converted by XLAT,
since XLAT only translates the header of the head skb. Consequently,
skbs in the frag_list may remain untranslated, resulting in protocol
inconsistencies and reduced throughput.

To address this, the patch explicitly sets the SKB_GSO_DODGY flag
for GSO packets in XLAT's IPv4/IPv6 protocol translation helpers
(bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6 and bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4). This marks GSO
packets as potentially modified after protocol translation. As a
result, GSO segmentation will avoid using skb_segment_list and
instead falls back to skb_segment for packets with the SKB_GSO_DODGY
flag. This ensures that only safe and fully translated frag_list
packets are processed by skb_segment_list, resolving protocol
inconsistencies and improving throughput when forwarding GRO packets
converted by XLAT.

Signed-off-by: Jibin Zhang <jibin.zhang@mediatek.com>
Fixes: 9fd1ff5d2ac7 ("udp: Support UDP fraglist GRO/GSO.")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260126152114.1211-1-jibin.zhang@mediatek.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c b/net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c
index fdda18b1abda..942a948f1a31 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c
@@ -107,7 +107,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *tcp4_gso_segment(struct sk_buff *skb,
 	if (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST) {
 		struct tcphdr *th = tcp_hdr(skb);
 
-		if (skb_pagelen(skb) - th->doff * 4 == skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size)
+		if ((skb_pagelen(skb) - th->doff * 4 == skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size) &&
+		    !(skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_DODGY))
 			return __tcp4_gso_segment_list(skb, features);
 
 		skb->ip_summed = CHECKSUM_NONE;

diff --git a/net/ipv4/udp_offload.c b/net/ipv4/udp_offload.c
index 19d0b5b09ffa..589456bd8b5f 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/udp_offload.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/udp_offload.c
@@ -514,7 +514,8 @@ struct sk_buff *__udp_gso_segment(struct sk_buff *gso_skb,
 
 	if (skb_shinfo(gso_skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST) {
 		 /* Detect modified geometry and pass those to skb_segment. */
-		if (skb_pagelen(gso_skb) - sizeof(*uh) == skb_shinfo(gso_skb)->gso_size)
+		if ((skb_pagelen(gso_skb) - sizeof(*uh) == skb_shinfo(gso_skb)->gso_size) &&
+		    !(skb_shinfo(gso_skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_DODGY))
 			return __udp_gso_segment_list(gso_skb, features, is_ipv6);
 
 		ret = __skb_linearize(gso_skb);

diff --git a/net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c b/net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c
index effeba58630b..5670d32c27f8 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c
@@ -170,7 +170,8 @@ static struct sk_buff *tcp6_gso_segment(struct sk_buff *skb,
 	if (skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST) {
 		struct tcphdr *th = tcp_hdr(skb);
 
-		if (skb_pagelen(skb) - th->doff * 4 == skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size)
+		if ((skb_pagelen(skb) - th->doff * 4 == skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size) &&
+		    !(skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_DODGY))
 			return __tcp6_gso_segment_list(skb, features);
 
 		skb->ip_summed = CHECKSUM_NONE;
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/net/core/filter.c b/net/core/filter.c
index 616e0520a0bb..bcd73d9bd764 100644
--- a/net/core/filter.c
+++ b/net/core/filter.c
@@ -3353,6 +3353,7 @@ static int bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6(struct sk_buff *skb)
 			shinfo->gso_type &= ~SKB_GSO_TCPV4;
 			shinfo->gso_type |=  SKB_GSO_TCPV6;
 		}
+		shinfo->gso_type |=  SKB_GSO_DODGY;
 	}
 
 	bpf_skb_change_protocol(skb, ETH_P_IPV6);
@@ -3383,6 +3384,7 @@ static int bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4(struct sk_buff *skb)
 			shinfo->gso_type &= ~SKB_GSO_TCPV6;
 			shinfo->gso_type |=  SKB_GSO_TCPV4;
 		}
+		shinfo->gso_type |=  SKB_GSO_DODGY;
 	}
 
 	bpf_skb_change_protocol(skb, ETH_P_IP);

The patch modifies three files to fix a GSO segmentation issue when forwarding GRO frag_list packets after protocol translation (XLAT). The key changes and their relationships are:

- **`net/core/filter.c`**: In both `bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6` and `bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4`, after adjusting GSO type bits during IPv4↔IPv6 translation, the `SKB_GSO_DODGY` flag is added to the GSO type. This marks the skb as potentially problematic because only the head skb's header is translated while frag_list entries remain untranslated.

- **`net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c`**, **`net/ipv4/udp_offload.c`**, **`net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c`**: In the GSO segmentation functions (`tcp4_gso_segment`, `__udp_gso_segment`, `tcp6_gso_segment`), the condition that decides whether to use the optimized frag_list segmentation path (`__tcp4_gso_segment_list`, `__udp_gso_segment_list`, `__tcp6_gso_segment_list`) is extended: it now additionally checks that `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is **not** set. If the flag is present, the code falls back to regular segmentation (linearization for UDP, or normal GSO for TCP), avoiding the unsafe frag_list path.

**Relationship**: The flag set in `filter.c` is consumed by the segmentation logic in the offload files. When a GRO packet has been transformed by XLAT, the `SKB_GSO_DODGY` flag is set. This prevents the kernel from using the `skb_segment_list` code path, which would incorrectly assume all frag_list entries have the same protocol header as the head skb. Instead, the fallback to `skb_segment` ensures that each fragment is fully translated, resolving protocol inconsistencies and restoring throughput.

### Summary of Modifications

#### Modifications in Each File

1. **`net/core/filter.c`** (BLP helper functions):
   - In `bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6()` – after changing `SKB_GSO_TCPV4` to `SKB_GSO_TCPV6` in the gso_type, the flag `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is explicitly set (`shinfo->gso_type |= SKB_GSO_DODGY`).
   - In `bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4()` – similarly, `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is set after converting `SKB_GSO_TCPV6` to `SKB_GSO_TCPV4`.

2. **`net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c`** (TCPv4 GSO segmentation):
   - In `tcp4_gso_segment()` – the condition for calling `__tcp4_gso_segment_list()` (the optimised frag_list path) now additionally requires that the `SKB_GSO_DODGY` flag is **not** set (`!(skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type & SKB_GSO_DODGY)`). 3. **`net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c`** (TCPv6 GSO segmentation):
   - In `tcp6_gso_segment()` – identical addition: the condition for `__tcp6_gso_segment_list()` now also checks that `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is absent.

4. **`net/ipv4/udp_offload.c`** (UDP GSO segmentation):
   - In `__udp_gso_segment()` – the condition for using `__udp_gso_segment_list()` (UDP frag_list GSO) is similarly extended to require that `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is not set.

#### Relationships Between Changes

The patch addresses a bug where GSO packets forwarded via XLAT (BPF-based protocol translation, e.g., IPv4→IPv6) have inconsistent headers: the head skb’s protocol is translated, but the skbs in the `frag_list` remain in the original protocol. This causes incorrect segmentation when the optimised `skb_segment_list()` path is used, leading to reduced throughput.

The **core insight** is to mark such translated packets as “dodgy” (`SKB_GSO_DODGY`) in the XLAT helpers (`filter.c`). Then, in the GSO segmentation entry points for TCP (IPv4 and IPv6) and UDP (`tcp_offload.c`, `tcpv6_offload.c`, `udp_offload.c`), the condition that selects the `__*_gso_segment_list()` fast‑path is tightened: **only** packets that are **not** dodgy (i.e., not modified by XLAT) may use the frag_list segmentation. All dodgy packets fall back to the safer `skb_segment()` path, which fully segments each fragment individually and guarantees protocol consistency.

Thus, the changes form a **coherent safeguard**: XLAT sets the flag, and the segmentation code respects it to avoid the buggy fast‑path when the frag_list is unreliable.

## Summary of Modifications

This patch fixes a bug in GSO segmentation of frag_list GRO packets after protocol translation (XLAT). The issue arises because `skb_segment_list` cannot correctly handle GRO skbs with a frag_list when only the head skb's header is translated, leaving frag_list skbs untranslated and causing protocol inconsistencies and throughput drops.

### Modifications per File

**1. `net/core/filter.c`**  
- In `bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6()` and `bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4()`:  
  Added `shinfo->gso_type |= SKB_GSO_DODGY;` for GSO packets. This marks the skb as potentially modified (dodgy) after protocol translation, indicating that the usual fast-path segmentation via `skb_segment_list` may be unsafe.

**2. `net/ipv4/udp_offload.c`**  
- In `__udp_gso_segment()`:  
  Modified the condition that decides whether to use `__udp_gso_segment_list()` for UDP frag_list GSO. Previously it only checked geometric consistency (`skb_pagelen() - sizeof(*uh) == shinfo->gso_size`). Now it also requires that the `SKB_GSO_DODGY` flag is **not** set (`!(shinfo->gso_type & SKB_GSO_DODGY)`). If the flag is set, the code falls back to `__skb_linearize()` and the generic `skb_segment()` path.

**3. `net/ipv4/tcp_offload.c`**  
- In `tcp4_gso_segment()`:  
  Similar change for TCPv4: the condition for taking `__tcp4_gso_segment_list()` now additionally checks that `SKB_GSO_DODGY` is absent. Otherwise, it proceeds with the fallback (setting `CHECKSUM_NONE` and letting `skb_segment` handle it).

**4. `net/ipv6/tcpv6_offload.c`**  
- In `tcp6_gso_segment()`:  
  Identical change for TCPv6: add the same `!(shinfo->gso_type & SKB_GSO_DODGY)` check to the condition guarding `__tcp6_gso_segment_list()`.

### Relationships Between the Modifications

- **Cause and Effect**: The changes in `net/core/filter.c` are the *trigger* – they set the `SKB_GSO_DODGY` flag on packets that have undergone protocol translation (XLAT), indicating that the frag_list may not be fully translated.  
- **Protection in Segmentation**: The changes in the three GSO segment functions (`udp_offload.c`, `tcp_offload.c`, `tcpv6_offload.c`) are the *safeguard* – they check for the `SKB_GSO_DODGY` flag and bypass the problematic `skb_segment_list` fast path when the flag is set. Instead, they fall back to the safe, generic `skb_segment()` path, which correctly handles potentially inconsistent frag_list entries.  
- **Together**, these two parts ensure that after XLAT translation, GSO packets with a frag_list are not processed by the fast segmentation path that assumes uniform headers across all fragments, thus fixing the protocol inconsistency and restoring normal throughput.

        net: fix segmentation of forwarding fraglist GRO

This patch enhances GSO segment handling by properly checking
the SKB_GSO_DODGY flag for frag_list GSO packets, addressing
low throughput issues observed when a station accesses IPv4
servers via hotspots with an IPv6-only upstream interface.

Specifically, it fixes a bug in GSO segmentation when forwarding
GRO packets containing a frag_list. The function skb_segment_list
cannot correctly process GRO skbs that have been converted by XLAT,
since XLAT only translates the header of the head skb. Consequently,
skbs in the frag_list may remain untranslated, resulting in protocol
inconsistencies and reduced throughput.

To address this, the patch explicitly sets the SKB_GSO_DODGY flag
for GSO packets in XLAT's IPv4/IPv6 protocol translation helpers
(bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6 and bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4). This marks GSO
packets as potentially modified after protocol translation. As a
result, GSO segmentation will avoid using skb_segment_list and
instead falls back to skb_segment for packets with the SKB_GSO_DODGY
flag. This ensures that only safe and fully translated frag_list
packets are processed by skb_segment_list, resolving protocol
inconsistencies and improving throughput when forwarding GRO packets
converted by XLAT.
